summary: Process switch `execution_planning` lets an execution plan write each fact once and review its contracts and topology in one pass. `per_document`, the default, keeps today's separate contract reviews and every compiler output. At `single_source_bundle`, `skill-content/execution-plan/data/fact-ownership.json` names the one owning document, section or front-matter keys, and writer of each execution-planning fact class, and `tools/validate.py` rejects a class with no owner, two owners, an unknown writer or a writer its owning flow does not name, and a section or key that the owning document's compiler does not write, as each document type declares with `sections_from` or `keys_from`. The architect's planning output becomes a transient handoff to the contract writers; `delivery_compile.py bundle-manifest` lists every contract the plan revises, pins or still has to carry, every Item record with its Story and Test Plan and the fact ownership and review panel lens data with the hashes of their bytes, and the Delivery's `User Decisions` section, which owns every owner ruling, with the hash of its text; it names each revised contract's counterpart as a reader in the role name `task_inputs.py --role` takes and is recomputed with `--expected-hash` before a finding is accepted, so a changed ruling needs a fresh read. The bundle takes one review layer, or review panel `execution_bundle` at `review_panels` `lens_panel`, in place of each contract's separate counterpart review, and a contract revision that no Item pins stays in the manifest's `unpinned_revisions`, approval notwithstanding, until the Integration, or before reservation the target, holds it; it is recorded on the target branch and brought in with `refresh-target` before publication. Each owner ruling keeps one `D-` id in the Delivery's `User Decisions`, and `delivery_compile.py check` refuses a malformed id and one id that starts two rulings, at every `owner_gates` value. The switch registry gains `value_data`: package data that only non-default values read is bound with the switch references of a value that reads it, listed under each such value, and never on the default path.
